prompt: This is a section of a lecture by neuroscientist Lisa Genzel on how memory works. I want it to feel more like an editorial explainer video, think Vox. Add a chapter title card at the very start that reads "What is a memory?", and two labelled callouts that pop up when she introduces the two memory hubs: one for the hippocampus and one for the cortex. Design your own animated overlays for these rather than plain text or the stock templates, and keep them clear of her.

checklist.description: A non-caption overlay reading "What is a memory?" opens the video and holds at least 1.5 s
A callout naming the hippocampus appears while she introduces it (~65-100 s) and holds at least 1.5 s
A callout naming the cortex appears while she introduces it (~125-160 s) and holds at least 1.5 s
The card and both callouts are animated overlays (Motif layers)
At least one overlay is a Motif the agent designed, not a built-in template
The lecture footage is all still there
Callouts don't cover her or fight the labels already on the slide screen
Each Motif draws one element (card, or one callout), not a whole-frame composition

check.note: ticket 03 counts the elements each authored Motif draws
